title: I Forwarded the Knitting-Meetup Yarn Raffle After They Drew Twice

parts.text: I bought one raffle ticket at 7:10 p.m. The host drew twice for the same skein and kept the second pull. The raffle card she read aloud said: ONE DRAW PER TICKET. HOST TICKETS LAST. I was fifty-one, new member, holding ticket 18. Host Nell said, "Hosts quality-check the skein." I pointed at the card. She pocketed the merino. "Quality lives here." I photographed the two stubs, the card, and the pocket. Then I forwarded the photo to the meetup email on the card. At 7:16 the co-host asked why Nell's name was on a double-draw ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The co-host can see two stubs for one skein against the card Nell read.

social.video_title: The host drew twice and pocketed the merino — Part 1/2
social.description: Ticket 18, a quality-check pocket, and a card read aloud. I forwarded the meetup email. Would you have clapped?

parts.text: Nell called it a tangle until the stubs matched two of her numbers. I printed the ticket, the card, and the photo. The skein went back in and drew once. Nell told the circle the card was always about optics. Optics is a word hosts use when merino is in a still. Raffle policy now has a second line: QUALITY DOES NOT POCKET. I buy one. Nell draws last. The bowl finally has one hand.

social.video_title: Quality does not pocket the merino — Part 2/2
social.description: Double-draw ticket, a real single pull, and a second line on the card. Was a tangle ever two stubs?
